sources.ar-SA-x-rijal-alma: Alfaifi 2024, Open Book Publishers 0411, ch. 5, citing Asiri 2008: spoken in the south-west of Saudi Arabia
sources.ar-SA-x-tihama-qahtan: Alqahtani 2015, A sociolinguistic study of the Tihami Qahtani dialect in Asir, quoting Johnstone 1967: South-western Arabian dialect group
sources.ar-TD-x-babalia: NOT FOUND: ISO 639-3 retired bbz (change request 2019-013, 2020-01-23), and Glottolog retired baba1273 as non-existent
sources.ar-TR-x-kinderib: NOT FOUND: needs Jastrow, which the papers library does not hold; Glottolog has no Kinderib languoid
sources.ca-x-alguer: Recasens, Fonètica històrica del català (IEC), p. 11: the conquest of Alghero in the mid-14th century, later than and separate from the medieval stage
sources.ca-x-balear: Recasens, Fonètica històrica del català (IEC), p. 11: Jaume I conquered the Balearic Islands with settlers mainly from eastern Catalonia, Roussillon and Occitania (1230-1235)
sources.ca-x-medieval: Recasens, Fonètica històrica del català (IEC), p. 10: before the conquest of the Balearic Islands and Valencia, Catalan had two dialects, eastern and western
sources.ca-x-nord: NOT FOUND: Recasens p. 10 names Roussillonese among the current dialects, but no source gives its medieval parent
sources.ca-x-occident: NOT FOUND: Recasens p. 10 names North-Western Catalan among the current dialects, but no source gives its medieval parent
sources.ca-x-valencia: Recasens, Fonètica històrica del català (IEC), p. 11: the conquest of Valencia with settlers mainly from western Catalonia and Aragon (1230-1250)
